hadith:
Mortgaging - Narrated `Aisha:

The Prophet (ﷺ) bought some foodstuff on credit for a limited period and mortgaged his armor for it.
message: All provisions in this life—whether wealth, food, or sustenance—flow from Allah, Al-Wahhaab (The Giver of All), reminding us to trust in His generosity and remain grateful. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) willingly mortgaged his possessions to meet genuine needs, we too should use our resources wisely and selflessly for what truly matters. This teaches us that reliance on Allah combined with honest effort and gratitude is the path to spiritual fulfillment.
name:
Al Wahhaab - الْوَهَّابُ - The Giver of All

The origin of Al Wahhaab comes from the Arabic root word 'wahb', which means to give or to donate freely. This name reflects the aspect of Allah's mercy and benevolence, emphasizing that all provisions and resources come from Him. In Islamic tradition, it is a reminder for believers to be grateful for God's endless gifts.
verse:
As-Saffat - Those who set the Ranks - 37:93

Then he swiftly turned on them, striking ˹them˺ with his right hand.
